dedupe_keys.name: road network map patch dataset generator

description: This Python package generates image patches from road-network map inputs for machine-learning experiments. Its README shows a MapReader loading a layered San Francisco map, then a MapsDataset sliding a 32 by 32 patch window with a chosen stride and writing sample groups as Dill objects. The repository also includes readers for reloading patches and source modules for OSM and map-image conversion. A modeller could use the patches to train or compare road-layout extraction or graph-generation methods, provided the source map is suitable for the intended city. The repository publishes an example layered map file, but the README does not document its date, accuracy or source licence; this review does not present that file as a verified city network. No package was installed, no patches were generated and no values were checked. The software is MIT-licensed according to GitHub metadata and the public licence file. Geographic coverage is controlled by the user’s input, not a built-in worldwide collection. Related resources are the underlying road-network maps and any separately published benchmark labels. The producing organisation named in the repository is Augmented Design Lab; the README does not name the provider of its example San Francisco map.
licence: MIT for software; source road-map data rights are not documented in the README.
